_comment: Tier-2 for fourc::thermo_transient_mms#4 — on a fixed mesh the error against the exact MMS solution saturates at the spatial Q1 floor, so a dt-halving table built from it stops measuring the time integrator; Richardson differences on the SAME mesh cancel the floor and recover the temporal order. Six dt levels on one 32x32 mesh at theta=0.5: the error-vs-exact sequence stops moving (ERROR_VS_EXACT_SATURATES=yes) and its apparent orders leave the neighbourhood of 2 entirely, going negative as the error starts to GROW with smaller dt (ERROR_VS_EXACT_ORDER_MISLEADING=yes), while every Richardson order sits in [1.9,2.1] (RICHARDSON_RECOVERS_ORDER_2=yes). A four-level backward-Euler series is the control: the same Richardson procedure returns ~1 there (RICHARDSON_SEPARATES_THE_SCHEMES=yes), so it is measuring the scheme and not returning 2 by construction. All nodal values are read out of 4C's own result-test lines (1089 per run, 'Checking results of 1089 tests:'), no post-processing library involved. Verified by execution 2026-08-06 against 4C 2026.2.0-dev (git 89519cf) at /home/alexander/4C/build/4C; wall time ~110 s.

_mutation.note: remove the pathology: stop pushing the dt series below the spatial floor. With only the three coarse levels the error-vs-exact table is still falling, ERROR_VS_EXACT_SATURATES flips to no and the fixture must go red.

make the control arm stop being a control: run it at theta=0.5 too. Richardson then returns ~2 for both, RICHARDSON_SEPARATES_THE_SCHEMES flips to no, and the fixture must go red — this is what proves the grader reads the scheme rather than the constant 2.
